title: The Gospel of Jesus Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The Gospel of Jesus Christ is the good news that God saves sinners through the death, burial, and resurrection of His Son. Because all people have sinned and fall short of God’s glory, salvation comes only by God’s grace through faith in Christ, not by human merit, religious effort, or self-rescue.
summary: The Gospel of Jesus Christ is the good news that God saves sinners through the death, burial, and resurrection of His Son. Because all people have sinned and fall short of God’s glory, salvation comes only by God’s grace through faith in Christ, not by human merit, religious effort, or self-rescue.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the center and substance of the Gospel. He lived without sin, died for sinners, rose from the dead, and gives eternal life to all who believe in Him. The Gospel is not merely advice for better living; it is the saving announcement of what God has done in Christ.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Gospel begins with the holiness and love of God. God created people for Himself, but sin has separated humanity from Him. Every person has sinned, and no one can make themselves righteous before God by works, morality, religion, recovery, knowledge, or effort. The human problem is deeper than weakness or brokenness alone; sinners need forgiveness, righteousness, reconciliation, and new life.

The good news is that God has acted in Jesus Christ to save sinners. Jesus died for our sins according to the Scriptures, was buried, and was raised on the third day. His death was not an accident or merely an example of courage. He gave Himself as the saving sacrifice for sinners, bearing guilt, satisfying justice, and opening the way for mercy.

The resurrection of Jesus proves that His sacrifice was accepted, His victory is real, and His promise of eternal life is sure. The Gospel announces that salvation is not earned but received by faith. Those who trust in Christ are forgiven, justified, made alive, and brought into peace with God.

There is no other Gospel. Any message that removes sin, weakens the cross, denies the resurrection, replaces grace with works, or makes Christ less than Savior and Lord is not the biblical Gospel. The church must guard the Gospel, proclaim the Gospel, live in the hope of the Gospel, and call all people to repent and believe in Jesus Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Without the Gospel, people are left trying to save themselves from a condition they cannot cure. Some try to overcome guilt through good works. Some try to numb shame through addiction, approval, success, religion, or distraction. Some believe they are too far gone to be restored. The Gospel speaks directly into all of that: sinners are worse off than they imagined, but Christ is a greater Savior than they dared to hope.

The Gospel also keeps Christian ministry centered. The church does not exist merely to inspire people, entertain people, improve behavior, or offer vague spirituality. The message entrusted to God’s people is Christ crucified, risen, and able to save. This good news brings hope to the guilty, the broken, the ashamed, the rejected, the addicted, the disabled, the suffering, and the religiously exhausted.

studySections.heading: Discipleship & Application
studySections.content: Receive the Gospel personally, not merely as information but as the truth on which your life depends. Turn from self-trust, hidden sin, religious pride, and hopelessness, and come to Christ in faith. Let the Gospel shape your worship, your repentance, your testimony, your forgiveness of others, and your mission. When you teach, counsel, preach, encourage, or serve, keep bringing people back to Jesus Christ—crucified, risen, and sufficient to save.
